preamble: A voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] palatalizing to a voiced (lamino-)postalveolar affricate [d͡ʒ] before front vowels. The only documented case found is Vâsi-vari (Prasun), Nuristani, where Strand, following Morgenstierne (1949), describes retroflex stops palatalizing in the environment of front vowels (ṭ > č, ḍ > ǰ). Strand's ǰ is a lamino-alveolar affricate, close to but not identical with IPA [d͡ʒ].

examples.note: 'drum'; cf. Kâmviri mâṇ'ü. The parallel voiceless change gives ič'i 'bone' (cf. Kâta-vari âṭ'i).

sources: Strand, R. F. (2026). The Evolution of the Nuristâni Languages. Nuristân: Hidden Land of the Hindu-Kush. https://nuristan.info/Nuristani/NuristaniEvolution.html
